A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same MLCL multilingual tool-calling study. The main text, Table 1, figures, and Appendices A and B can be reliably matched despite pagination changes.

before.justification: v1 reports original multilingual tool-calling experiments, error distributions, mitigation evaluations, and model-scale and perturbation analyses in Sections 3–4 and Appendix B.

after.justification: v2 retains these original experimental results, including the benchmark comparisons, mitigation outcomes, and appendix analyses.

M1.justification: MLCL construction and the prompt-level instruction (PT), pre-translation (PRE), and post-translation (POST) procedures remain unchanged in Section 4.2 and Appendix A.3.

E1.justification: Both use the same BFCL V4 single-turn, multiple-candidate-function subset, covering English, Chinese, Hindi, and Igbo under the same translation and semantic-perturbation scenarios.

E2.justification: Table 1 retains the same GPT-5, DeepSeek V3.2, Llama 3.1, Qwen 3, and Granite 4 variants. Model and mitigation-strategy participation in the corresponding comparisons is unchanged.

E3.justification: Sections 3.2–3.3 retain the same query-generation procedures, English-only execution interface, BFCL exact-matching evaluation, and error-attribution protocol. No experimental setting is revised.

E4.justification: The semantic-perturbation tests, translation-induced semantic-drift case study, and model-scale and architecture analyses are retained. Appendix B adds no new robustness test or supplementary analysis.

E5.justification: Statistical reporting is unchanged. v2 adds no repeated-run counts, seed information, uncertainty intervals, or significance tests.

E6.justification: The result plots in Figures 4–7 and Appendix B retain the same data and findings. The translation case study and reported model rankings are also unchanged; relocated plots introduce no new result entries.

T1.justification: The task formulation, execution assumptions, and error-category definitions are unchanged. Neither version presents formal theorems or proofs.

C1.justification: The abstract, contribution list, and conclusion retain the same claims about MLCL, parameter-value language mismatch, and the inability of the tested mitigation strategies to consistently restore English-level performance.

C2.justification: The interpretations concerning execution-interface constraints, translation-induced drift, and low-resource language comprehension remain unchanged. The Limitations section retains the same applicability boundaries.

D1.justification: Appendix A retains the same code/data access information, prompts, manual verification process, and model-specific I/O documentation. New acknowledgments credit API and computing support without adding implementation settings or access instructions.

R1.justification: Five references are added in the Introduction and Related Work, spanning uncertainty/calibration, alignment, and multilingual evaluation. The surrounding arguments and positioning of the research gap remain unchanged.

P1.justification: v2 adds an Acknowledgment section before Limitations and makes small wording, punctuation, and capitalization edits. The substantive narrative and section organization remain intact.

P2.justification: Figure 1 receives revised icons, capitalization, and function-call line wrapping. Existing appendix figures are redistributed across pages, while Table 1 and the remaining figure content are retained.

improvement.justification: The additional citations and acknowledgments expand attribution, and Figure 1 receives cosmetic polish. These limited editorial updates leave the scientific argument, empirical support, limitations, and reproducibility documentation essentially unchanged, producing no meaningful net difference in overall paper quality.
